tasks.short: Prepare and deliver advertising sales presentations that win or expand customer business.

steps.what: Collect account history, campaign results and opportunity details from the {CRM}.
Adapt approved presentation material to the customer's goals and proposed advertising programme.

loop.input: Presentation facts, approved slides, performance evidence and customer objectives.
loop.output: A populated presentation with tailored narrative and source references.
loop.check: Validate figures against source fields; restrict claims to approved evidence; check required slides and layout.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; missing evidence or failed layout checks go to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can populate figures, but tailoring the narrative across varied customer briefs needs language drafting.

steps.what: Review the proposal, claims and presentation narrative before customer use.
Arrange the presentation with customer stakeholders.
Present the programme, explore objections and agree the next commercial discussion.
Record customer reactions and follow-up commitments in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Pull presentation facts from the {CRM} into approved templates in the {DOCS}, with deterministic figure checks and one bounded narrative-drafting loop. Configure booking through the {CALENDAR} and a short outcome form in the {CRM}; the seller approves the presentation and leads the customer discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sellers repeatedly copy facts into decks, while customer-specific storytelling makes a single fixed presentation inadequate.
tasks.enabler_now: Document generation and record integration handle repeatable assembly. Bounded drafting can adapt approved material without giving a model control of the sale.
tasks.still_hard: A persuasive presentation depends on stakeholder priorities, credible evidence and handling objections live. Poor source data still produces a weak deck.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, build a persuasive commercial story and adapt the discussion when stakeholders disagree.

ambition.what: Offer tailored campaign reviews to smaller existing advertisers previously receiving only generic materials.

tasks.altitude: The seller arrives with more preparation time available for stakeholder strategy and rehearsal. Presentation support does not expand discount or contract authority.

reach.task: Plan stakeholder coverage for an account expansion.
reach.learn: Buying-group mapping, executive sponsorship and opportunity qualification.

evidence.claim: Customer-record-filled templates and bounded drafting can support sales materials; this digest provides no measured presentation case.
Human delivery remains the largest component of this task; deck automation alone does not automate the customer discussion.

assumptions: Approved presentation templates and reusable campaign evidence exist.
Live delivery remains the majority of time, consistent with the supplied priors.
Booking is limited to seller-selected contacts and offered time slots.
The seller enters meeting outcomes directly; recording and transcription are unnecessary.
Build ranges assume reuse of shared customer-data connections.
unknowns: How much presentation material is reusable and approved.
Whether campaign results can be reliably linked to customer records.
Which booking and document-generation features are already available.
Which employee consultation and access approvals apply under national rules.
research_questions: Which deck sections require tailoring and which should remain fixed?
Can generated decks pass factual and visual checks with a single repair pass?
new_work: Review generated narratives, charts and claims.
Maintain presentation templates and approved examples.
Resolve missing or inconsistent campaign figures.
Keep stakeholder lists and outcome-form fields useful.
tasks.statement: Prepare and deliver sales presentations to new and existing customers to sell new advertising programs and to protect and increase existing advertising.

tasks.short: Explain which advertising formats suit a customer's goals and why.

steps.what: Review customer goals and campaign history in the {CRM}.
Read media descriptions and prepare explanations suited to the customer's objectives.

loop.input: Customer context and approved media descriptions and performance evidence.
loop.output: Cited talking points explaining relevant formats and their limitations.
loop.check: Require a source for each factual claim; distinguish observed results from forecasts.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported claims or missing evidence return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply facts, but adapting explanations to varied customer goals needs language interpretation.

steps.what: Choose suitable formats and assess trade-offs against the customer's objectives.
Explain the recommendation, answer objections and agree realistic expectations with the customer.
Send the customer a written recommendation and agreed next steps.

tasks.design: Configure a customer context view in the {CRM} and use a bounded drafting loop over approved material in the {DOCS}. The seller chooses the recommendation and conducts the conversation; a configured {EMAIL} template assembles selected formats, expectations and next steps for approval before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Media descriptions, customer history and supporting results sit in separate places. Tailoring an explanation still takes reading and writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record views and templates handle assembly. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while a bounded model call can draft cited explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Advertising outcomes depend on creative quality, audience and execution. Evidence may be weak or incomparable, and confident wording can overstate effectiveness.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's actual constraints, challenge unrealistic expectations and earn trust while explaining uncertain outcomes.

ambition.what: Review the channel mix at each campaign milestone using fresh results.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time finding and rewriting product facts and more time discussing trade-offs. No new commercial decision rights arise automatically.

reach.task: Validate tracking and delivery requirements for a proposed advertising format.
reach.learn: Measurement limits, attribution assumptions and technical feasibility checks.

evidence.claim: Approved-document retrieval, cited explanations and human handoff are plausible support patterns; recommendation quality remains unproven here.
Teamleader combines customer records and quotes, with its Focus AI acting after approval; this supports the gated workflow pattern.

assumptions: The baseline represents a typical mid-size European advertising seller, not a measured customer workflow.
Conversation remains the largest time component, consistent with the supplied priors.
Approved media descriptions and usable performance evidence exist.
Build ranges are working effort, not elapsed procurement or consultation time; shared foundations reduce duplication across tasks.
No call recording or employee scoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which media formats are sold and how current their evidence is.
Whether the {CRM} supports the required views and approved email templates.
The lawful basis, access permissions and retention rules for customer information.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Which explanation claims can be traced to approved evidence?
Does the preparation aid reduce time without increasing unsupported promises?
new_work: Review drafted talking points and outbound summaries.
Maintain approved claims, evidence dates and media descriptions.
Handle customer situations that do not fit the available evidence.
Maintain access controls and source links.
tasks.statement: Explain to customers how specific types of advertising will help promote their products or services in the most effective way possible.

tasks.short: Maintain advertiser relationships, develop accounts and agree next commercial actions.

steps.what: Review account history, open opportunities and renewal dates.
Read recent correspondence and assemble an account brief.

loop.input: Account-linked correspondence, campaign reports and account activity summary.
loop.output: A short account brief with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate account identifiers and source references; the seller checks commercial meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; missing or conflicting facts become questions for the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Client priorities and concerns sit in free text. Structured account fields supply the factual backbone.

steps.what: Choose accounts to contact and set meeting objectives.
Discuss campaign performance, business needs and upcoming advertising plans.
Agree campaign objectives, responsibilities and next commercial actions.
Update account records and write the campaign brief.
Send the follow-up and arrange agreed meetings or internal actions.

tasks.design: Configure account views, structured meeting notes and action templates in the {CRM}, linked to {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}. A bounded drafting loop prepares source-linked briefs from approved correspondence in {EMAIL} and reports in {DOCS}. The seller chooses priorities, leads client conversations and approves external follow-ups.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account context was scattered across records and correspondence. Useful preparation required reading, while relationship decisions resisted fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing account views and workflow configuration handle most administration. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records, while a bounded loop handles correspondence.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution, agency relationships and changing advertiser priorities remain uncertain. GDPR and national rules affect access to correspondence and changes to employee activity tracking.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unstated concern, repair trust after a weak campaign and judge when to ask for more business.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on which at-risk advertiser renewals need a recovery meeting.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reconstructing account history toward recovery conversations and campaign planning. Within existing delegation, the seller chooses recovery meetings and standard follow-up actions; pricing authority does not expand.

reach.task: Triage renewal risks across a small account portfolio.
reach.learn: Revenue concentration, renewal forecasting and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Develop a structured account growth plan.
reach.learn: Stakeholder mapping and discovery beyond the current advertising purchase.

evidence.claim: Account views, structured notes and configured follow-ups can reduce account administration without automating relationship decisions.
Teamleader combines CRM records and online quote signing, and its Focus AI acts after approval.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The baseline represents a mixed portfolio of recurring advertisers and developing accounts.
Human conversations account for half the task; the communication-heavy prior is retained.
The target uses typed notes rather than introducing call recording or seller scoring.
Consultation and access ranges include national employee consultation where applicable; they are not statutory deadlines.
unknowns: Whether account correspondence and campaign reports can be linked reliably to account identifiers.
Which account views, templates and integrations are already licensed and configured.
The seller's actual authority over recovery actions and commercial concessions.
Whether proposed activity tracking requires national employee consultation.
research_questions: Which account facts are repeatedly reconstructed before meetings?
Does a source-linked brief change meeting preparation time or renewal decisions?
Which structured note fields preserve useful context without increasing administration?
new_work: Review account briefs and correct misleading summaries.
Resolve unmatched correspondence and stale renewal dates.
Maintain note templates, access permissions and follow-up rules.
tasks.statement: Maintain assigned account bases while developing new accounts.

tasks.short: Process account correspondence, prepare paperwork, and pass accepted advertising bookings to operations.

steps.what: Read incoming account correspondence and identify the required action.

loop.input: Account correspondence and attachment text.
loop.output: Suggested action, extracted references and a source-linked summary.
loop.check: Validate the action against allowed categories and require source spans for extracted facts.
loop.stop: One pass and one validation retry per message; ambiguous requests enter the seller's exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules handle known senders and document types, but free-text requests mix changes, questions and acceptance.

steps.what: Match the correspondence to the correct customer and opportunity.
Check booking, billing and contact fields for completeness.
Fill standard booking forms, agreements and account letters from approved templates.
Resolve missing information and disputed terms with the customer.
Check commercial authority and approve the final paperwork.
Send approved paperwork to the customer for acceptance.
File the correspondence, issued paperwork and customer acceptance against the account.
Enter accepted booking details and billing references in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Connect the {EMAIL}, {CRM}, {DOCS} and {ERP} through the {WORKFLOW}, using identifiers, required fields and approved document templates. A bounded model classifies unfamiliar correspondence; deterministic checks match records, generate paperwork and prevent duplicate bookings. The authorised approver clears commercial commitments before sending, and customer acceptance must be verified before an accepted booking reaches the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Free-text requests obscured otherwise structured transactions. Missing identifiers and different booking fields made manual copying the practical fallback.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can turn correspondence into reviewable suggestions. Existing configuration and faster connector development handle the structured work without autonomous agents.
tasks.still_hard: Commercial exceptions, legal wording and uncertain customer acceptance need people. GDPR requires appropriate access, purpose and retention controls for correspondence.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a negotiation from acceptance and resolve disputed commitments without losing the customer relationship.

ambition.what: A guided first-booking paperwork service for small advertisers without an agency.

tasks.altitude: The seller handles exceptions and first-booking support instead of copying fields. Standard bookings can progress within delegated limits; contract exceptions and credit decisions retain their existing approvers.

reach.task: Validate an advertising booking before billing and production.
reach.learn: Booking identifiers, customer acceptance evidence, billing references and duplicate prevention.

reach.task: Approve commercial exceptions.
reach.learn: Discount authority, unusual cancellation terms and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Teamleader supports customer records and online quote signing; its Focus AI acts after approval.
Templates, field validation and idempotent integrations can automate standard account paperwork without an agent.
The effort shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

assumptions: The reference process covers routine correspondence through accepted booking; not every message creates an order.
Exact identifiers permit automatic matching. Ambiguous matches and nonstandard acceptance evidence require review.
The authorised sales approver is the seller within delegated limits and the sales manager for exceptions.
The time split includes the order clerk's final handoff work.
Build ranges cover one booking route. Access and employee consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: The actual contract, discount, credit and booking approval limits.
Whether the {CRM} and {ERP} expose supported interfaces and shared identifiers.
Which customer acceptance methods are valid for each agreement type.
The volume of amendments, cancellations, unmatched messages and duplicate records.
Applicable retention periods, access permissions and national employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which correspondence categories can be recognised reliably enough to reduce review?
Which acceptance checks prevent false booking creation across different document formats?
new_work: Review ambiguous correspondence, record matches and customer acceptance evidence.
Maintain templates, required fields and approval routing.
Resolve rejected transfers and reconcile bookings between the {CRM} and {ERP}.
Review permissions, retention settings and connector failures.
tasks.statement: Process all correspondence and paperwork related to accounts.

tasks.short: Send advertising proofs, explain them, and capture customer approval against the correct version.

steps.what: Retrieve the latest proof and match it to the campaign brief.
Check the proof for obvious errors and consistency with agreed requirements.
Send the checked proof with approval instructions and a deadline.
Explain the proof and discuss customer questions or requested changes.
Record customer approval or changes against the exact proof version.
Forward the approved version or requested changes to the creative team.

tasks.design: Configure a version-specific approval flow in the {WORKFLOW}, linking proofs in the {DOCS} to campaigns in the {CRM}. The seller checks the proof and recipient before the {EMAIL} request leaves; the customer explicitly approves that version or requests changes. Reminders and the creative handoff follow recorded status, while explanatory conversations remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attachments, customer replies and production deadlines were disconnected. Reliable version control required more coordination than sending an attachment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval flows can provide version links, reminders and audit records. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting metadata and status; no model is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous replies, replacement proofs and delegated customer authority still need attention. Visual correctness and the meaning of requested changes remain human judgements.
tasks.human_edge: Explain creative choices, notice hesitation and resolve disagreements without treating silence as approval.

ambition.what: A scheduled proof clinic for first-time advertisers before their first publication deadline.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time chasing replies and locating versions, leaving room for first-time advertiser support. Publication and customer approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Release an approved advertising booking to production.
reach.learn: Version identifiers, publication cut-offs and the difference between approval and a change request.

evidence.claim: Version-specific approval requests, reminders and status-based handoffs can use deterministic workflow configuration.
The effort shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

assumptions: Proofs have stable campaign and version identifiers.
The reference workflow includes substantive customer discussion; simple repeat proofs may need none.
Customer approval uses an explicit version-specific action; email exceptions return to the seller.
Build ranges are working effort for one pilot workflow. Access and any employee consultation under national rules can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether the existing {WORKFLOW} supports external approvals and immutable proof versions.
Who may approve for each customer and how delegation is verified.
How often approval arrives through email, telephone or an agency.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Does a version-specific approval link reduce clarification without confusing occasional customers?
Which proof metadata checks can prevent wrong-version delivery reliably?
new_work: Maintain approval templates, customer permissions and escalation deadlines.
Handle ambiguous replies, expired links and replacement proofs.
Review failed reminders and missing creative handoffs.
tasks.statement: Deliver advertising or illustration proofs to customers for approval.

tasks.short: Prepare advertising agreements, obtain signatures and coordinate collection of payments.

steps.what: Gather agreed campaign details, prices and billing information.
Populate the advertising agreement from the approved contract template.
Discuss requested changes to campaign commitments, cancellation terms or payment dates.
Approve commercial exceptions within delegated limits or escalate for legal review.
Check the final agreement and send it for advertiser signature.
Create and send the invoice after the contractual billing trigger.
Match bank receipts to invoices and identify overdue balances.
Send routine payment reminders for undisputed overdue invoices.
Discuss disputed invoices or missed commitments and agree the next collection action.

tasks.design: Validated deal fields from the {CRM} populate approved templates in the {DOCS}; configured approvals and the {ESIGN} control agreement release. The signed agreement and billing trigger feed the {ERP}, where configured reconciliation matches receipts from the {BANK} and routes ambiguous matches to finance review. The {ERP} sends policy-based reminders through {EMAIL}, suppressing disputed invoices and leaving negotiation with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales, signature and finance records were disconnected. Nonstandard clauses and payment disputes made the whole task appear inseparable from human judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Template generation, signature workflows, reconciliation and reminders are established capabilities. AI-assisted coding makes missing field mappings and validation cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Nonstandard liability, cancellation disputes, campaign underdelivery and uncertain payment references need judgement. GDPR, confidential contract access and national contract rules still apply.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate a fair resolution while protecting the advertiser relationship and the company's commercial position.
tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time assembling agreements and chasing routine balances, with more time for disputed commitments and account recovery. Decision rights over discounts, credits and legal terms do not change.

reach.task: Validate the handoff from agreed campaign to billable order.
reach.learn: Billing triggers, order identifiers and duplicate-invoice prevention.

reach.task: Prepare a recommendation on a commercial contract exception.
reach.learn: Margin exposure, cancellation risk and delegated approval limits.

evidence.claim: Teamleader supports CRM records and quotes signed online; its Focus AI acts after approval.
Structured deal fields and approved clauses support deterministic agreement generation without a drafting model.
Invoice generation, bank matching and reminder schedules are established finance-system configuration patterns.
The supplied evidence does not establish end-to-end advertising contract or collection savings; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: Prices and campaign terms have been agreed before contract preparation; this task does not create new pricing authority.
The baseline includes the surrounding finance handoffs because collecting payment crosses roles.
Time shares are blended across routine agreements and exceptions; exception approval is conditional.
Receipt review covers ambiguous matches; exact matches can post under approved rules.
Routine reminders use an approved schedule and stop when payment, a dispute or a payment commitment is recorded.
Consultation and access estimates include national employee consultation where the change affects employee monitoring.
unknowns: Whether signed agreement fields and billing triggers can pass reliably into the finance records.
Which contract amendments need commercial approval, legal approval or both.
Whether bank matching and reminder functions are already available and configured.
How campaign delivery affects billing, disputes and collection holds.
Who may approve credits, revised payment terms and collection escalation.
research_questions: Which contract fields are re-entered between sales, signature and finance?
Which existing configuration can replace manual work before custom integration is built?
What causes unmatched receipts and inappropriate reminders?
Which exception types account for most negotiation and collection effort?
new_work: Maintain approved clauses, field mappings and billing-trigger rules.
Review agreements before signature requests and assess commercial exceptions.
Resolve ambiguous receipts and failed invoice handoffs.
Maintain dispute holds, payment commitments and reminder policies.
Check for duplicate invoices and inconsistent contract versions.
tasks.statement: Draw up contracts for advertising work, and collect payments due.

tasks.short: Find suitable prospective advertisers, check contact permissions and start commercial conversations.

steps.what: Search public business directories for potential advertisers.
Check existing records and remove duplicate or already assigned prospects.
Read business websites to assess advertising fit and a useful contact reason.

loop.input: A fixed set of permitted public business pages and explicit target account criteria.
loop.output: A prospect brief with fit reasons, supporting sources and uncertainty.
loop.check: Require a source for each business fact; exclude unsupported need, budget and personal inferences.
loop.stop: At most five pages and one model pass per prospect; inaccessible or ambiguous cases return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Business descriptions vary in free text. Exact industry and location filters run before this step.

steps.what: Check contact permissions, suppression records and permitted communication channels.
Write a relevant introductory message using the available advertising offer.

loop.input: Reviewed prospect brief, approved media facts and an approved outreach structure.
loop.output: One short introductory message.
loop.check: Check factual claims against inputs; reject unsupported performance promises, rates and personalisation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; failed checks fall back to the approved template.
loop.why_not_simpler: A relevant opening sometimes needs paraphrasing business context; standard introductions use templates directly.

steps.what: Send the introductory message to the selected prospect.
Call eligible prospects to explore interest and qualify a possible campaign.
Record the response, qualification outcome and follow-up date.

tasks.design: A deterministic import on the {DATA_PLATFORM} brings permitted business listings into the {CRM}, removes duplicates and checks channel eligibility against maintained rules. Bounded loops prepare source-linked prospect briefs and optional message drafts; configured {EMAIL} sending requires seller approval and a fresh eligibility check. Human calls through the {TELEPHONY} feed a short structured qualification form in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prospect research was fragmented, contact rules were checked manually and relevant introductions took time to write. Sending more messages did not solve qualification or trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured deduplication, deterministic eligibility checks and small integrations handle the repeatable work. Bounded reading and drafting handle varied business descriptions without autonomous outreach.
tasks.still_hard: Public contact details do not establish permission to market. GDPR, national channel rules, data licensing and uncertain commercial fit remain constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Earn attention, handle objections and distinguish polite interest from a genuine advertising opportunity.

ambition.what: Relevant local businesses outside the existing advertiser referral network.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends more time on qualified conversations and less time searching and copying records. They gain a clearer choice of eligible prospects; authority over pricing and campaign commitments stays unchanged.

reach.task: Run permission-aware first-contact qualification calls.
reach.learn: Channel eligibility, concise discovery and respectful objection handling.

reach.task: Evaluate which prospect segments create viable opportunities.
reach.learn: Cohort conversion, acquisition effort and selection bias.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales has a qualification agent that researches leads, judges fit and sends outreach.
The Netherlands requires prior opt-in for calls to consumers, sole traders and general partnerships from 1 July 2026, including existing customers.
Dutch guidance allows calls to specified corporate legal forms subject to identification and other calling requirements; this is not a Europe-wide rule.
Deduplication and explicit channel rules can run deterministically; uncertain eligibility can block contact for manual resolution.
Research and record checking can occupy more time than the supplied meeting-heavy prior suggests; the proposed shares require observation.

assumptions: Prospecting includes desk research, an initial message and a qualification call; not every prospect reaches every stage.
Listing access is permitted and does not depend on bypassing website restrictions.
Unknown contact eligibility blocks outreach; a model cannot infer consent.
The target introduces no AI caller, call recording or seller scoring.
Consultation and access ranges include national employee consultation where activity tracking changes.
unknowns: Which countries, legal forms and communication channels the team targets.
Whether permission evidence, objections and suppression records are complete.
Which listing sources permit the intended access and reuse.
Whether existing configuration already supports deduplication and approval before sending.
research_questions: Which prospect facts predict useful conversations without speculative personal profiling?
How much research can existing filters eliminate before a model reads business pages?
Which eligibility checks need legal interpretation before becoming maintained rules?
Does researched outreach improve qualified responses enough to justify its data and review costs?
new_work: Maintain country-specific channel rules and suppression synchronisation.
Review prospect briefs and outbound message drafts.
Resolve uncertain legal forms, identities and permissions.
Monitor source changes, data quality and prospecting costs.
tasks.statement: Locate and contact potential clients to offer advertising services.

tasks.short: Calculate advertising estimates and explain their price, assumptions and conditions to customers.

steps.what: Read the customer's advertising request and identify missing specifications.

loop.input: Customer email and attached advertising specifications.
loop.output: Structured requested formats, quantities, dates, budget and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate field types, units and catalogue identifiers; link extracted values to source text.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction; ambiguous specifications return to the seller without inferred values.
loop.why_not_simpler: Email requests use inconsistent language and attachments; fixed parsing cannot reliably map them to quote fields.

steps.what: Clarify formats, dates, quantities and budget with the customer.
Check the rate card for relevant formats, quantities and production charges.
Check placement availability and delivery constraints in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate the estimate, including discounts, production charges and applicable taxes.
Approve any discount or commercial term outside delegated limits.
Prepare the customer estimate with prices, validity dates, assumptions and exclusions.
Check and send the estimate with an explanation of its assumptions.

tasks.design: Configure a price catalogue and estimate templates in the {CRM}, with a deterministic calculator and a read-only availability connection to the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A bounded loop extracts emailed requests; the seller confirms specifications, exceptions route through the {WORKFLOW}, and approved estimates are sent through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rates, placement availability and discount decisions are disconnected. Variable customer requests create manual rekeying before otherwise routine arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Most of the solution uses established catalogue, calculation and approval patterns. AI-assisted coding lowers integration effort; a small extraction loop handles free-text requests.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke packages, negotiated rates and fast-changing inventory need careful versioning. Availability checks do not reserve inventory, and an estimate must make that distinction clear.
tasks.human_edge: Clarify what the customer actually needs, negotiate fair commercial terms and decide whether an unusual concession is worthwhile.

ambition.what: Provide a same-conversation comparison of three feasible advertising packages.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time calculating and assembling estimates and more time comparing options with the customer. Existing discount limits remain the basis for decision rights.

reach.task: Validate an accepted estimate before creating the advertising order.
reach.learn: Placement identifiers, production deadlines, order completeness and billing handoff requirements.

evidence.claim: Agentforce for Revenue is described as building a quote from a typed sentence.
Salesforce reports 75% less quoting time and 87% fewer clicks in its own sales team; the digest gives no baseline or period.
A rate-card calculator with discount limits can handle standard advertising estimates without model-based arithmetic.

assumptions: The baseline uses a spreadsheet rate card to connect sales and operations; system-native quoting is also common.
The approval step is an average across a mix of standard and exceptional estimates.
The {CRM} supports a configurable catalogue and document templates; otherwise a small deterministic records app is needed.
Prices, tax treatment, units and approval limits can be expressed as maintained rules.
Quoted build effort assumes one pricing scheme and one operations connection, without inventory reservation.
unknowns: Whether rates and discounts already exist in a configurable quoting module.
How much seller time is actually spent calculating versus discussing estimates.
Whether the {OPS_SYSTEM} exposes reliable availability data.
Which packages require bespoke pricing or production review.
Who can approve discounts and how long estimates remain valid.
Which access approvals and national employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can historical estimates be reproduced exactly from versioned pricing rules?
Which missing specifications most often cause rework?
What availability freshness is sufficient for a non-binding estimate?
new_work: Maintain versioned prices, tax rules and discount limits.
Review extracted specifications and final customer estimates.
Handle bespoke packages and unavailable inventory.
Monitor failed connections and stale availability data.
Test pricing changes against representative historical estimates.
tasks.statement: Provide clients with estimates of the costs of advertising products or services.

tasks.short: Recommend advertising sizes and formats that fit the advertiser's objectives, medium and practical constraints.

steps.what: Read the advertiser's request and clarify objectives, budget and creative constraints.

loop.input: Campaign brief and advertiser correspondence.
loop.output: Structured objectives, medium, dates, budget and creative constraints.
loop.check: Require source references for extracted values; validate dates, currencies and required fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; ambiguous or missing requirements return to the seller.
loop.why_not_simpler: Advertisers describe requirements in free text. Existing structured fields are reused without model processing.

steps.what: Look up current format specifications and creative submission requirements.
Compare eligible sizes and formats against objectives and budget.
Check candidate formats against available advertising inventory and production deadlines.
Explain trade-offs and agree the preferred format with the advertiser.
Send the recommended media plan and creative specifications.

tasks.design: Keep versioned media specifications and eligibility rules in the {DOCS} and a small rules service on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop turns mailed requirements into fields; deterministic code produces a comparison using approved rates and availability from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A configured {CRM} template assembles the media plan for seller approval and delivery through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications, rate cards and inventory were maintained separately. The seller had to translate informal requests into comparable options.
tasks.enabler_now: A small rules service and document templates are inexpensive to build and connect. Free-text extraction can be bounded by required fields and source checks.
tasks.still_hard: Creative suitability and likely audience response are not fully specified by eligibility rules. Availability can change between recommendation and booking.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why a technically valid format may fail creatively, and uncover what the advertiser really needs.

ambition.what: First-time regional advertisers needing a simple, affordable format consultation.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time checking specifications and more time comparing creative trade-offs with advertisers. They can recommend standard eligible formats within existing authority; exceptions still need the relevant commercial or production approval.

reach.task: Translate campaign requirements into a technically feasible media configuration.
reach.learn: Constraint modelling, inventory limitations and production validation.

reach.task: Show how the same creative works across advertising formats.
reach.learn: Creative examples, visual explanation and medium-specific limitations.

evidence.claim: Format eligibility, dimensions, deadlines and approved rate calculations can be encoded as deterministic rules.
Free-text requirements can be extracted into a checked schema while creative suitability remains subject to seller review.
No supplied source documents this exact advertising-format solution; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The baseline uses documents for specifications, a comparison workbook and an operations screen for inventory.
Technical eligibility is more rule-covered than creative suitability; the latter retains human review and conversation.
Availability checks do not reserve inventory or promise delivery.
Consultation and access estimates include national employee consultation if the implementation changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Whether specifications and rate cards have authoritative owners and effective dates.
Whether inventory can be read through an interface or only through exports.
Which formats require production review before a recommendation.
Whether creative examples contain restricted client material or personal data subject to GDPR.
research_questions: Which format decisions follow stable rules, and which depend on creative judgement?
How often do outdated specifications cause rejected creative or rework?
Can existing configuration provide the comparison before custom code is needed?
new_work: Maintain specification versions, eligibility rules and approved examples.
Review extracted requirements and unusual recommendations.
Handle stale availability and production exceptions.
Check that generated plans use the correct specification version.
tasks.statement: Recommend appropriate sizes and formats for advertising, depending on medium used.

tasks.short: Explain advertising artwork options and provide suitable samples.

steps.what: Ask about the customer's message, audience, assets and artwork budget.
Find current artwork specifications, service options and approved samples.
Select relevant examples and assemble an options sheet.
Explain examples, production trade-offs and the customer's preferred direction.
Send selected samples, specifications and next steps.
Record the chosen direction and artwork follow-up.

tasks.design: An approved catalogue in the {DOCS} tags samples by format, service level, usage rights and production constraints. tasks.altitude: The seller handles fewer scheduling exchanges and arrives better prepared. Attendance and customer care still dominate the task, and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Coordinate a production supplier against an agreed service scope.
reach.learn: Cancellation terms, production dependencies and when a scope change requires fresh approval.

evidence.claim: Availability collection, constraint checks and call-sheet generation can use deterministic workflows.
Customer accompaniment and live production concerns require human presence and situational judgement.

assumptions: Studios and customers can respond through a scheduling form or structured availability options.
Routine reminders and call sheets may be sent within an approved session workflow.
Booking approval time is counted in slot selection; the booking action carries the approval gate.
Time shares and build ranges are pilot estimates. Formal consultation under national rules may take longer.
unknowns: Whether the seller or production coordinator owns studio bookings today.
Whether studio availability can be read electronically.
Which bookings create cancellation charges or require supplier approval.
How much attendance time includes travel.
Which access and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which constraints cause most failed scheduling attempts?
Can the booking flow prevent confirmations against stale availability?
Which session changes need customer approval rather than a routine update?
new_work: Resolve unavailable slots and late cancellations.
Maintain studio constraints, charges and instruction templates.
Correct contact details and failed calendar invitations.
Enter live session decisions without recording or scoring conversations.
tasks.statement: Arrange for commercial taping sessions, and accompany clients to sessions.

tasks.short: Write sales outlines that help staff explain advertising offers and handle common objections.

steps.what: Gather current product facts, audience evidence, prices and sales policies.
Review recent sales feedback for questions and recurring objections.

loop.input: Permitted sales feedback and selected customer correspondence.
loop.output: Objection themes linked to source examples, with customer details minimised.
loop.check: Validate source references and counts; seller checks grouping and removes misleading examples.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction; uncertain items remain unclassified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customers express the same concern in varied language; fixed keywords miss or merge important distinctions.

steps.what: Write a sales outline with discovery questions, benefits, evidence and objection responses.

loop.input: Approved source pack, objection themes and an outline template.
loop.output: A sourced sales outline with questions, benefit statements and permitted responses.
loop.check: Verify prices against the rate card and claims against sources; seller checks usefulness and tone.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims are omitted and flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but adapting explanations and responses to a sales context needs contextual writing.

steps.what: Review commercial accuracy and approve the outline for staff use.
Publish the approved outline and notify staff of the current version.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles approved facts from {DOCS} and {CRM}; bounded loops classify objections and draft a sales outline. Deterministic checks validate prices, source references and required sections. After sales manager approval, {WORKFLOW} publishes the exact approved version in {DOCS} and sends an internal notice through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts and feedback are dispersed, and every update requires manual gathering, rewriting and distribution.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned source retrieval and workflow configuration handle assembly and release. Bounded models can turn varied feedback into a reviewable outline.
tasks.still_hard: A polished outline may teach weak selling habits or overstate evidence. Selecting useful questions and credible responses still requires sales experience.
tasks.human_edge: Experienced sellers know which questions reveal a real buying problem and which responses sound evasive or overpromising.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of the objection response to test in sales coaching.

tasks.altitude: The seller spends less time compiling documents and more time testing their usefulness with colleagues. They can recommend coaching experiments; the sales manager retains approval of official guidance.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of non-retail sales workers
reach.task: Coach staff using a selected discovery question or objection response.
reach.learn: Role-play facilitation, feedback quality and evaluating observed sales behaviour.

evidence.claim: Source-based drafting, rule checks and approval-triggered publication can support sales outline production.
The supplied digest contains no documented sales-outline case supporting a measured productivity claim.

assumptions: Approved product facts, rate cards and policies have identifiable current versions.
Feedback is analysed to improve guidance, without recording calls or scoring individual employees.
The high automation prior applies mainly to assembly and drafting; commercial approval remains a distinct decision.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Permissions and any consultation required by national rules are included in the access range.
A personal starter can work from approved source files before shared integrations are available.
unknowns: Who approves official sales guidance?
Which feedback and correspondence may be reused?
How are obsolete prices and claims withdrawn?
Which national employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which outline sections do staff actually use during preparation?
How should coaching tests distinguish useful guidance from changes in lead quality?
new_work: Review objection groupings and unsupported claims.
Maintain source ownership, expiry dates and outline templates.
Withdraw outdated versions and collect staff feedback.
Evaluate coaching experiments before changing official guidance.
tasks.statement: Write sales outlines for use by staff.

Better preparation supports existing authority; broader pricing or account rights require explicit delegation.

Sales engineer: advertising measurement and delivery feasibility.
Sales representative of services: structured discovery and qualification.
Order clerk: clean conversion from accepted estimate to executable order.

Conduct discovery that exposes objectives, constraints and buying dynamics.
Compare advertising packages using versioned prices and realistic assumptions.
